title: Symmetric monoidal localization of a tensor-stable system
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], enlarging the ambient universe if necessary. Let $\mathcal C^{\otimes}$ be a symmetric monoidal infinity category, encoded by a cocartesian fibration over $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ whose fiber over the pointed set $\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$ is identified by the inert projections with $\mathcal C^n$; inert means each non-basepoint of the target has exactly one preimage. Let $W$ be a collection of arrows of $\mathcal C$ containing all equivalences, closed under composition and homotopy, such that $X\otimes w$ and $w\otimes X$ lie in $W$ whenever $w\in W$ and $X\in\mathcal C$. There exist a symmetric monoidal infinity category $\mathcal D^{\otimes}$ and a strong symmetric monoidal functor $q^{\otimes}:\mathcal C^{\otimes}\to\mathcal D^{\otimes}$ with the following properties. Its underlying $q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is the homotopy coherent localization at $W$: restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal E)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$ carrying $W$ to equivalences, for every infinity category $\mathcal E$. For every symmetric monoidal $\mathcal E^{\otimes}$, restriction similarly identifies the infinity category of strong symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathcal D^{\otimes}$ to $\mathcal E^{\otimes}$ with the full subcategory of those from $\mathcal C^{\otimes}$ carrying $W$ to equivalences. In particular
$$q(X)\otimes q(Y)\simeq q(X\otimes Y),\qquad \mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\simeq q(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}),$$
with coherent associativity, unit and symmetry constraints. This applies in particular to the symmetric monoidal nerve of an ordinary symmetric monoidal category.
